answer: In an agent market trading saffron, quill pens, and relic replicas, each voting identity must lock 100 tokens in escrow for 30 days, and each bond buys exactly one vote. Creating extra accounts yields no extra influence unless the attacker funds a separate bond for each one. Controlling 1,000 votes therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month, making influence costly in capital even when fake identities are free to create.
